CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is used to style and layout web pages. It allows you to control the appearance of HTML elements, including colors, fonts, spacing, and overall design.

## What is CSS?

CSS is a stylesheet language that describes how HTML elements should be rendered on screen, in print, or other media. It separates the presentation of a document from its structure, making it easier to maintain and update the look and feel of a website.

## Basic CSS Syntax

```css
selector {
    property: value;
}
```

In this syntax:
- `selector` is the HTML element you want to style.
- `property` is the CSS property you want to modify.
- `value` is the value for that property.

For example, to change the color of all paragraphs to blue, you would write:
```css
p {
    color: blue;
}
```
This will apply the blue color to all `<p>` elements on the page. You can also target specific elements using classes and IDs for more precise styling.
```css
/* Targeting elements with a class */
.my-class {
    font-size: 18px;
}
/* Targeting an element with an ID */
#my-id {
    background-color: yellow;
}
```
